sources.title: Human History Map: indexed East Prussia and decoded 1920/1930 geometry
sources.note: Own-project index and decoded border files, checked locally. See identities.json and geometry-checks.json. The 1920 southern omissions are not treated as accurate historical boundaries.

sources.title: Geheimes Staatsarchiv: Kingdom of Prussia and province of East Prussia, 1701 to 1945
sources.note: Direct institutional text checked. Use administrative chronology and archival holdings; do not repeat its oversimplified assertion that Versailles affected only Memel.

sources.title: East Prussian State Museum: National history
sources.note: Direct full exhibition account checked, especially Weimar isolation, Nazi persecution and the province’s destruction and population displacement.

sources.title: City of Olsztyn: History
sources.note: Direct official city history checked: hospital 1867, railway 1872, utilities, 1920 plebiscite, capture in 1945. Avoid treating its general Warmia sentence as every village voting identically.

sources.title: US State Department: 1945 briefing on East Prussia, attachment to document 513
sources.note: Indexed full original attachment read: after Versailles German sovereignty but physically separated; boundaries fixed 16 August 1920 after plebiscites. Its 1945 recommendations are not cited as completed decisions; contested ethnicity counts are not repeated.

sources.title: Maria Dembińska: Jakie źródło, taka woda, in Olsztynek museum Zeszyty Naukowe 8 (2017)
sources.note: Downloaded institutional PDF and directly extracted selected text. Printed pages 110 to 111 share human PDF page 56. The article distinguishes original structures, replicas and museum arrangements. Nowe Kawkowo interior explicitly represents the 1920s and 1930s; no claim all objects stayed in original locations.

sources.title: Museum of Warmia and Masuria: Maselnica na biegunach (2025)
sources.note: Full indexed original museum entry read; object dated 1880, from near Pisz, wooden rocking churn without nails. Modern price jokes in source not used.

sources.title: Masurian Museum in Szczytno: Kultura ludowa Mazurów
sources.note: Full indexed original permanent-exhibition description checked. Published 2010, updated 2023; objects collectively illustrate traditional regional household crafts, but individual object dates generally absent. Public text keeps this as retrospective material context.

sources.title: Olsztyn Water and Sewerage Company: History
sources.note: Full indexed official text checked. Epidemics motivated 1893 water project; construction began 1897; pump/treatment rebuilding 1927 to 1935. No assertion that safe water reached every household.

sources.title: State Archive in Olsztyn: Municipal infrastructure in Warmia and Masuria before 1945
sources.note: Direct full original text: water, sanitation and caption 15 for late nineteenth-century toilet advertisements; 1898 Shone pneumatic system; Pisz lacked modern sewer enterprise in 1945.

sources.title: Yad Vashem: Album of a Jewish school in Königsberg
sources.note: Direct full museum account checked; Kaelter family archive P.46, school founded 28 April 1935 with 82 pupils, family gatherings, Nazi pogrom and 1942 deportations. All passages charged to this one work.

sources.title: Gazeta Olsztyńska, no. 260, 6 November 1924, page 1
sources.note: Original four-page digitized issue downloaded and page 1 rendered and visually inspected. Masthead GAZETA OLSZTYŃSKA and printed date 6 listopada 1924 verified. Title given in ordinary title case; literal English translation supplied. Editorial nationality statistics not adopted as neutral evidence.

sources.title: Museum Dom Gazety Olsztyńskiej: Exhibitions
sources.note: Direct exhibition listing checked: Polish schools in Warmia and Masuria, 1929 to 1939, preserving Polish identity; Gazeta Olsztyńska 1886 to 1939. Listing only, not a full pupil census or classroom inspection.

sources.title: Wolfgang Fiedler: Wann und wohin? Vogelwanderungen auf der Spur, Max Planck Yearbook 2006/2007
sources.note: Indexed original PDF text checked, printed page 2/8: Thienemann from 1901 developed large-scale marking at Rossitten after Mortensen’s early success. Avoid sole-inventor claim; broader modern research statistics not backdated. HTML and PDF are one work.

sources.title: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum: Poland in 1945
sources.note: Indexed original museum account checked: southern East Prussia assigned to Poland, Soviet retention of formerly Polish eastern territory, Potsdam border settlement.

sources.title: East Prussian State Museum: History of the museum
sources.note: Direct institutional history read: refugees and expellees, Lüneburg, hunting museum founded 1958, rebuilt collections and widening later historical remit.

proposedOverrides.name: East Prussia
proposedOverrides.summary: A Baltic province of Prussia and Germany, shown in an incomplete interwar atlas window.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct provincial card; no alias with Prussia, Germany, Poland, Lithuania, occupied Polish territories or displaced communities.
batchIdentityNotes.map: Indexed 1920 to 1938. Southern omissions in 1920 and Rossitten omission in both are public. Memel and Danzig excluded; later annexations not smuggled into the interwar outline.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Original 6 November 1924 newspaper masthead visually read; Polish Latin alphabet, title case normalization and literal translation.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceLimits: Museum reconstruction and retrospective collection evidence explicitly distinguished from unchanged original interiors. Copernico ending essay blocked and not used; Yad Vashem article, not every attachment, directly read.
